style: Simple 2.5D scientific illustrations for the Cells README

assets.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a simple README header/logo for the open-source scientific simulator Cells.
Create an elegant, very simple 2.5D logo on a clean white background. Landscape banner, approximately 2.5:1. Combine a compact mark of three softly rounded, adjoining biological cells with the word "Cells" in large, beautifully spaced dark sans-serif lettering. The three cells suggest communication and a small tissue; one tiny nucleus per cell, and a small connection between neighbouring cells. Restrained shallow depth, matte surfaces, a few soft shadows; mostly clean flat shapes. Keep the silhouette memorable and the mark legible when reduced to a small README header. Leave generous white space around everything. Scientific and friendly, without cartoon faces or decorative complexity. Use a restrained cool scientific colour treatment, with dark high-contrast text. The only text is exactly "Cells". No slogan, GPU chips, arrows, technical labels, watermark, borders or extra objects. This is one finished logo banner, not a sheet of alternative concepts.

assets.purpose: Current capabilities and independent GPU ensemble architecture
assets.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: one simple landscape README infographic for the open-source Cells simulator, approximately 2.5:1 aspect ratio.
Primary request: explain current simulation capabilities and the independent-ensemble GPU architecture in an approachable 2.5D illustration with very little text.
Style: generous white space, clean white background, shallow matte 2.5D objects, soft restrained shadows, pale blue/teal/periwinkle, dark navy sans-serif text. Match a logo showing three softly rounded adjoining blue, teal and periwinkle biological cells beside the word Cells. Large readable labels; elegant and sparse rather than a complex technical poster.
Layout: title at top "Cells today". Beneath it, three small equally weighted capability illustrations: a cell membrane with ions labelled "Bioelectricity"; a cell with a few calcium signalling dots labelled "Calcium signalling"; a simple partially assembled protein cage labelled "Protein assembly". Beneath this, one clear left-to-right execution flow: a small stack of independent simulation cards labelled "Work queue", then arrows distributing cards to exactly four separate GPU chip icons, then arrows collecting outputs into a folder labelled "Results + checkpoints". The four chips together have one label "GPU workers". Label this execution row "Independent simulations". Each worker runs separate worlds; do not draw a single tissue divided among GPUs, or connections suggesting inter-GPU biological communication.
Two clear, prominent status labels below the flow, exactly "Verified locally: CPU + L4" and "Jupiter: qualification planned". The GPU array is the ensemble architecture, NOT a claim that a four-GPU Jupiter run has passed. Preserve this distinction visibly. No checkmarks over the four-chip array, no utilization percentages, no speed claims, no hardware brand logos, no extra captions. Render exactly the quoted text, including the plus signs. Keep the overall image simple and suitable for a GitHub README.

Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: one simple landscape future-roadmap infographic for the open-source Cells simulator, approximately 2.5:1 aspect ratio.
Primary request: a very simple 2.5D visual of future plans, with four spacious illustrated milestones and very little text.
Style: generous white space, clean white background, shallow matte 2.5D objects, soft restrained shadows, pale blue/teal/periwinkle, dark navy sans-serif text. Match a logo showing three softly rounded adjoining blue, teal and periwinkle biological cells beside the word Cells. Large readable labels; elegant and sparse rather than a complex technical poster.
Title exactly "Where Cells goes next". A clear small badge exactly "PLANNED".
One horizontal sequence of four similarly sized icons joined by thin subtle arrows:
1. A small cell membrane with a few different transport channels. Main label "BETSE coverage". Smaller label "More channels and transport".
2. A cell with a simple assembly cluster and energy symbol. Main label "Integrated biology". Smaller label "Assembly, energy and mechanics".
3. A compact group of GPU chips. Main label "Jupiter scaling". Smaller label "4 to 16 GPUs".
4. A small block of connected tissue gradually suggesting an organ shape, understated and schematic. Main label "Organ models". Smaller label "Tissue to organ function".
All four are future development goals, not completed features; the PLANNED badge should be unmistakable. No dates, timelines, checkmarks, performance percentages, claim of existing multi-node execution, extra slogans, watermark, vendor logos or elaborate technical details. Render only the quoted words and labels exactly. Make the diagram readable at a normal GitHub README width.

assets.purpose: Research goals: test Plastic Heredity and Forms in increasingly realistic cell and tissue models
assets.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: one finished landscape infographic for the open-source Cells scientific simulator README, approximately 2.5:1 aspect ratio, readable at normal GitHub page width.
Primary request: show that a central goal of Cells is to test the Plastic Heredity and Where Do Forms Come From? preprints in increasingly realistic cell and tissue simulations.
Style: simple, spacious 2.5D scientific illustration matching the other Cells README assets: white background, shallow matte forms with restrained soft shadows, pale blue, teal and periwinkle, high-contrast dark navy sans-serif typography. A few rounded biological cells with small nuclei; no faces. Generous whitespace, large labels, no technical clutter.
Layout: title at the top exactly "Why we are building Cells". Beside it a small but clearly legible badge exactly "RESEARCH GOALS".
Below, four equally spaced illustrated stages linked by three thin arrows, left to right:
1. Heading "Ask". Two simple manuscript cards, one labelled "Plastic Heredity" and the other labelled "Where Do Forms Come From?". Wrap the second title neatly onto two lines. No other text on the cards.
2. Heading "Model". A small connected tissue of softly rounded blue and teal cells, with only a few ion dots and internal structures. Caption exactly "Realistic cells and tissues".
3. Heading "Intervene". A tiny three-cell group with a fading cue arrow and a visibly interrupted connection, representing controlled experiments. Caption exactly "Remove cues and disrupt pathways".
4. Heading "Measure". Two small tissue arrangements with some cells pale and others coloured, suggesting comparison across replacement and reconstruction. Caption exactly "Memory, inheritance and form". Do not imply a successful result or show a quantitative plot.
Bottom caption, clear and compact, exactly "Increasing realism. Testing predictions."
Scientific constraints: This is a conceptual research programme, not evidence that the hypotheses are confirmed or that growth, turnover, mechanics or whole-organ biology have already been implemented. No success checkmarks, invented data, measured curves, percentages, proof claims, hardware/GPU diagrams, dates, vendor logos, watermarks or extra labels. Render only the quoted text accurately. Keep the overall design simple and coordinated with an understated scientific README.

edits.purpose: Rename the Forms preprint to How Forms Become Reconstructible
edits.prompt:
Use case: text-localization.
Asset type: edit the existing Cells README research-goals infographic.
Input image: the provided image is the edit target; preserve its overall design, dimensions and composition.
Primary request: the second manuscript has been renamed. Change only its title from "Where Do Forms Come From?" to exactly "How Forms Become Reconstructible", without a question mark.
Typography: keep dark navy sans-serif text on the right-hand manuscript card in the Ask panel. Wrap the new title naturally across three or four lines and reduce its size only as needed to fit legibly within that card. Spell "Reconstructible" exactly R-e-c-o-n-s-t-r-u-c-t-i-b-l-e. Keep the complete word intact on one line. A small adjustment to the card width or decorative grey lines is allowed if necessary for the longer title.
Invariants: preserve "Plastic Heredity" on the other card; preserve the main title "Why we are building Cells", the "RESEARCH GOALS" badge, "Ask", "Model", "Intervene", "Measure", all other captions and the footer "Increasing realism. Testing predictions.". Preserve the white opaque background, pale blue/teal/periwinkle cells, shallow 2.5D rendering, arrows, tissue illustrations, generous spacing and original landscape aspect ratio. Keep all other text and artwork unchanged as closely as possible. No new labels, scientific claims or decorative objects.

assets.purpose: Map animal-cell structures and processes to selected Cells simulation capabilities
assets.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: finished infographic for the open-source Cells simulator website and GitHub README.
Canvas: landscape 16:9, ideally 3840 x 2160. Light almost-white background, fully opaque.

Create a polished scientific infographic titled "From cell biology to Cells". Subtitle exactly "Connecting molecular assembly, cell physiology and tissue communication."

Brand style: match the existing Cells visual identity: clean white space, dark navy modern sans-serif typography, softly rounded scientific forms, matte 3D shading and restrained soft shadows, pale blue, teal and periwinkle. Make this image colorful with tasteful lavender, coral-orange, turquoise and blue organelles while retaining that calm, approachable Cells style. No dark background. This is an accessible website graphic with generous spacing, not a dense research poster.

Composition: one large biologically recognizable animal cell in the middle, seen in a realistic scientific 3D cutaway. It occupies about 42% of the width. The organelles should have anatomically plausible membranes, folds and relationships, rendered with real biological detail but the soft matte finish of the Cells brand. Include a turquoise plasma membrane with channel proteins, translucent pale blue cytoplasm, a lavender nucleus, folded lavender endoplasmic reticulum, coral-orange mitochondria with visible cristae, and a few blue protein complexes. A small sliver of a neighboring cell at the lower right shows a gap-junction connection. No plant structures. Molecular objects are schematic and enlarged for legibility.

Arrange exactly eight spacious callouts: four on the left and four on the right. Each is a small pale-tinted rounded card with a slim color accent, a small biological label, a larger bold Cells layer name, and a short explanation. Use clear large readable typography with careful line breaks. All words must remain entirely inside their card. Thin color-matched leader lines run from cards to small anchor dots on the relevant biological structure. Keep line routes legible and noncrossing; lines must never cross text. Organelles are arranged to support clear connections. Decorative leader lines have no directional arrowheads: they identify structures, not causal flows.

Left cards from top to bottom, EXACT text for each:
1. Small label "Cell membrane"
   Bold layer "Bioelectricity"
   Explanation "Membrane voltage, ion channels and pumps"
   Connect to plasma membrane channel proteins.
2. Small label "Cytoplasm"
   Bold layer "Chemistry and transport"
   Explanation "Reactions, diffusion and ion concentrations"
   Connect to cytoplasmic space.
3. Small label "Endoplasmic reticulum"
   Bold layer "Calcium signalling"
   Explanation "Calcium storage, release, uptake and IP₃"
   Connect to folded ER membranes.
4. Small label "ATP and cell volume"
   Bold layer "Fuel and water"
   Explanation "Finite energy supplies, osmosis and volume"
   Connect to small schematic ATP/water dots near the cell boundary.

Right cards from top to bottom, EXACT text for each:
1. Small label "Regulatory machinery"
   Bold layer "Regulatory cell state"
   Explanation "Selected gene and microRNA circuits"
   Connect to the nucleus and nearby molecular machinery.
2. Small label "Mitochondria"
   Bold layer "Organelle physiology"
   Explanation "Ion exchange and membrane voltage"
   Connect to a mitochondrion.
3. Small label "Protein complexes"
   Bold layer "Molecular assembly"
   Explanation "Formation, breakage and finite protein pools"
   Connect to one small partly assembled protein cage in the cytoplasm.
4. Small label "Cell contacts and surroundings"
   Bold layer "Tissue communication"
   Explanation "Gap junctions and extracellular fields"
   Connect to the neighboring-cell junction/extracellular interface.

A subtle pale-blue foundation strip at the bottom, with exactly:
"Python + JAX · CPU references · GPU execution"
"Conservation checks · Reproducible checkpoints"
Below it, one small but readable caption:
"Schematic mapping. Capabilities vary by model; whole-cell integration is ongoing."

Scientific scope: the image is a schematic mapping of biology to selected simulation capabilities, not a claim of complete whole-cell simulation. Do not imply that the nucleus is a whole-genome simulation, mitochondria already implement respiratory ATP production, or the protein cage represents all cellular assembly. No mitochondrial ATP arrows. No unsupported feature checkmarks, multi-GPU performance claims, extra organelles with software labels, or extra text.
Output one complete beautifully balanced infographic, all edges and text within safe margins. No watermark, stock-photo marks, website browser frame, or alternative panels.
